The present anticipatory bail application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. has been filed seeking anticipatory bail in case crime No.817 of 2022 under sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C., P.S.
Kotwali Sadar, district Lakhimpur Kheri.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned Additional Government Advocate for the State.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated.
The story narrated by the prosecutrix is entirely improbable.
The first information report has been lodged via application under section 156(3) CrPC.
Occurrence is of 14.6.2020, however, the first information report has been lodged by moving the said application on 25.2.2021.

In the first information report,
time of the incident has not been mentioned.
The alleged incident is said to have taken place on 14th June, 2020 as stated by the prosecutrix in her statement under section 164 CrPC.

sentences.text: It is next submitted that on the date of the incident, the applicant was on duty in Kanpur whereas the incident has taken place in district Unnao.
The duty chart as well as certificate are annexed with the affidavit filed in support of the application.
Learned Addl.

Government Advocate has, per contra, submitted that had it been a case of false implication, the victim would have roped in the entire family members, however, the allegation of rape is only against the applicant who happens to be brother in law of the victim.
It is further submitted that the victim has supported the prosecution case in her statement under sections 161 and 164 CrPC.
The plea of alibi taken by the applicant's counsel can be taken at the stage of trial and not at this stage.
Offence is quite serious.
The submission advanced by learned A.G.A. carries weight.
Offence is quite serious.
The victim has supported the prosecution case in her statement under sections 161 and 164 CrPC.
It is not a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
The application is dismissed.
